The *Nāgavimānavatthu* (Vv 41), translated as "Elephant Mansion", is a verse text included in the *Vimānavatthu* collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. It relates the story of a deity (*deva*) who, having offered a pair of robes to the Buddha in a previous life, reaped the karmic fruit of substantial celestial happiness [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].
No curated cross-language parallels are cataloged by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. However, computational text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus identifies 24 matching passages shared across three Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Most prominently, the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* incorporates 18 matching segments (most substantially §3.4–6.4) [DharmaNexus]. The text also exhibits substantial internal formulaic overlap with other *Vimānavatthu* texts, sharing passages with *Paṭhamanāgavimānavatthu* (Vv 60, segments §1.3–3.4) and *Pallaṅkavimānavatthu* (Vv 31, segments §2.4–3.4) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also indicates minor cross-language alignments with the Sanskrit *Ajitasenavyākaraṇa* (best score 25, segments §0.4–2.1), although these represent machine-computed text reuse rather than confirmed canonical parallels [DharmaNexus].
